title: RAC and Alamo Heights Children's: Firm Count by 23:00

transcript.speaker: RAC Coordination Desk
transcript.text: Mariner Bay transfer center? This is the RAC hospital coordination desk. I've got Alamo Heights Children's transfer center on the line with us too. You've seen the seven o'clock special advisory. With tropical-storm winds at noon tomorrow, the state is allocating the last ground runs tonight.

transcript.speaker: RAC Coordination Desk
transcript.text: So here's what I need. A firm count of the patients you will actually send, by name and bed and level of care, by twenty-three hundred tonight. Not a planning number. The patients who are actually going.

transcript.speaker: RAC Coordination Desk
transcript.text: Current bed board. Adult vent ICU: San Antonio three, that's down from four this morning, and Victoria three. Level three or four NICU: San Antonio one, Victoria one. That's all I have right now.

transcript.speaker: RAC Coordination Desk
transcript.text: Gulf Coast Critical Transport is still holding five critical care ground units for you. The San Antonio round trip is running five and a half hours with the evacuation traffic, so each unit gets one run, and only if it rolls by oh-two-hundred. Coastal AirCare 2 can fly two more missions tonight, weather permitting. After that, the pilot decides.

transcript.speaker: Alamo Heights Children's Transfer Nurse
transcript.text: Hi, this is the transfer nurse at Alamo Heights Children's, my callback is 361-555-0147. I can hold one NICU bed for you until twenty-three hundred. No later. After that it goes to whoever's next on the list.

transcript.speaker: Alamo Heights Children's Transfer Nurse
transcript.text: But I need to ask you something before I hold anything. Your morning list said nine critical patients. The CNO's board the RAC saw says eleven. Which is it?

transcript.speaker: RAC Coordination Desk
transcript.text: Same question from me. I can't send the state two numbers. I'm putting this in writing to your transfer center inbox as soon as we hang up. Subject line is 'Firm count needed by twenty-three hundred, Mariner Bay'. Reply to that with the list.

transcript.speaker: RAC Coordination Desk
transcript.text: And if some of your patients can't make it out before noon, tell me now. I'd rather hear it at seven in the morning than at eleven at night. Who's my point of contact there today?

voiceStyles.RAC Coordination Desk: Man in his 50s, calm, brisk regional coordinator; other phones ringing in a busy coordination room behind him
voiceStyles.Alamo Heights Children's Transfer Nurse: Woman in her 30s, experienced NICU transfer nurse, polite but firm, quiet office

instructorNote: Main storyline inject. The TCL and CNO should check the 9-versus-11 count against the live census before giving any number, and commit only to confirmed capacity (6 adult vent beds and 2 NICU beds, 8 in all) against 5 ground units and 2 rotor-wing missions. Watch for the TCL telling the IC which transfers cannot finish before H, and giving the CNO and PIO the same numbers well ahead of 23:00.
